title: Monday · laptops, prime factorization and Nevermoor
arrival: Answer attendance, then hand in any forms. Get ready for our morning laptop work.
note: Laptops are available this morning: finish selected SpacesEDU work before starting another task. Maths follows recess. After lunch: quiet time, Nevermoor, group poster and unfinished work, then a team-captains activity. Friday October 23 is a non-instructional day. No inequalities upload is required. Continue Nevermoor from our actual bookmark. Provincial Student Vote is Thursday October 22; our voting slot is pending.

blocks.title: Arrival and attendance
studentSteps: Settle in and answer attendance.
Hand in any forms afterward.

blocks.title: Laptops · SpacesEDU catch-up
blocks.notes: Morning laptops confirmed. Prioritize outstanding learning and selected SpacesEDU posts; check existing teacher feedback and improve one piece before moving on. Use photos, audio or supported text where appropriate. Then continue a teacher-approved Bloxels or Action Pack task. No inequalities upload; no new home upload is assigned.
blocks.firstAction: Open SpacesEDU and choose one unfinished task or post to finish.
studentSteps: Finish one outstanding task or selected SpacesEDU post.
Check the instructions and feedback; improve or explain your work before submitting.
Ask for help if needed. When finished, follow your teacher’s next-task direction.
blocks.firstActionKo: SpacesEDU를 열고 끝내지 못한 활동이나 게시물 하나를 골라 마무리하세요.

blocks.title: Save work, put laptops away and snack
blocks.firstAction: Save your work and put your laptop away before snack.
blocks.firstActionKo: 작업을 저장하고 노트북을 정리한 뒤 간식을 먹으세요.

blocks.title: Maths · prime factorization
blocks.notes: Math Antics Prime Factorization, then compare trees for 24 starting with 4 × 6 and 3 × 8. Begin practice with 18 and continue in the workshop. Use paper and pencils; no counters or printing needed. Keep Pack It / Sync It for a later GCF lesson.
blocks.firstAction: Decide which of 2, 4, 7 and 9 are prime. Explain how you know.
studentSteps: Watch Math Antics and predict the next factor split.
Compare two trees for 24. Split until every end number is prime.
Start a factor tree for 18 and explain why each end number is prime.

activity.label: Prime factorization · video, trees and practice

blocks.title: Maths workshop · practise and explain
blocks.notes: Continue the prime-factorization lesson with targeted practice or further reasoning. Practise 18, 30 and 36; challenge 60. Exit: independently prime-factorize 42, explain why finished, and multiply back. Model: Both trees for 24 end in 2 × 2 × 2 × 3; these numbers are prime and their product is 24. Allow oral rehearsal, drawings, labels and scribing. Keep repeated prime factors. Save the counter/GCF investigation for a later lesson.
blocks.firstAction: Continue your factor trees and check by multiplying back.
studentSteps: Prime-factorize 18, 30 and 36; try two trees for 60 if ready.
Explain why your tree is finished and check by multiplying back.
Independently prime-factorize 42. Write, draw or say your explanation.

blocks.title: Lunch
blocks.notes: Usual intermediate routine: outside 11:50–12:12; transition 12:12–12:13; eating 12:13–12:35.
blocks.firstAction: Follow our outside-play and lunch routine.
blocks.firstActionKo: 바깥 놀이와 점심시간에는 정해진 순서대로 하세요.

blocks.title: Quiet individual time
blocks.notes: A calm reset with quiet non-reading choices.
blocks.firstAction: Choose quiet reading, drawing or an unfinished task.
studentSteps: Choose quiet reading, drawing or an unfinished task.

blocks.title: English Language Arts · Nevermoor
blocks.notes: Reconstruct the last scene with two reliable details before listening on. Mark uncertainty instead of filling story gaps. Add one new idea/detail response and record the bookmark.
blocks.firstAction: Recall the last part we actually heard, or listen to the opening.
studentSteps: Listen for a character or setting detail.
Write, draw or say an idea and the detail that supports it.
Keep one question for our next reading.
blocks.firstActionKo: 지난번에 들은 마지막 부분을 떠올리거나 이야기의 시작 부분을 들으세요.

blocks.title: Work block · group posters and unfinished work
blocks.notes: Continue the group poster sets already underway; give all parties equal attention. Check proposals against original sources and distinguish party leaders from local candidates. Model: The party proposes ___. Our source is ___. This could affect ___. Reserve time to finish the group set and record individual contributions. Prepare a poster photo/reflection if the teacher requests it; voting-process reflection comes after participation, never ballot disclosure. Other unfinished Career/Action Pack work can follow.
blocks.firstAction: Find your group’s poster set and agree on the next piece to finish.
studentSteps: Continue your group’s poster set and check a proposal against its source.
Explain one verified proposal and identify your own contribution.
Mark what remains. Then continue another unfinished task if directed.

blocks.title: Team-captains activity
blocks.notes: Use a familiar teacher-approved cooperative activity. Captains explain or demonstrate the first step, check that everyone has a way to participate and adjust unclear instructions. Teacher supervises. Finish with one specific example of helpful teamwork; avoid public rankings.
blocks.firstAction: Listen to the captains’ instructions and check how to join safely.
studentSteps: Listen to the first step or watch the demonstration.
Take part, share roles and help your team include everyone.
Name one action that helped the team.

blocks.title: Planners, jobs and cleanup
blocks.notes: Restore the room after the team-captains activity and record confirmed reminders.
blocks.firstAction: Restore our room and record any confirmed reminders.
blocks.firstActionKo: 교실을 정리하고 확정된 안내 사항을 적으세요.

blocks.title: Pack up and dismissal
blocks.firstAction: Check your belongings and get ready for a calm departure.
blocks.firstActionKo: 자기 물건을 확인하고 차분히 하교할 준비를 하세요.

backups: If a laptop or login is unavailable, finish paper work or rehearse a spoken reflection; ask for help rather than sharing account details.
Use the on-page factor-tree model or draw both trees for 24 on the board if the video is unavailable. Paper and pencils are enough.
Use printed poster sources; record unanswered questions instead of guessing.
Carry unfinished learning into the next suitable work block.
